notes: Identity independently assessed: opening title is Reexamining the effect of gustatory disgust on moral judgment: A multi-lab direct replication of Eskine, Kacinik, and Prinz (2011); author list starts Eric Ghelfi, Cody D. Christopherson, Heather L. Urry and ends Dasan Sullivan, matching the assigned reference. The main text is a full author manuscript with Methods, Results, Discussion and appendix; its project URL https://osf.io/5ygsp matches the input. Appended published-version excerpts explicitly identify the same title and publisher DOI 10.1177/2515245919881152. The manuscript is a primary replication report, not a secondary commentary or preregistration. The published-version component is excerpts only, not a complete second version. No local PDF supplied; no rendering possible within the assigned files. The supplied neutral description establishes the bitter versus control moral-wrongness contrast, but does not select all participants versus political subgroups, meta-analysis versus LMER, small-telescopes versus equivalence null, or one of three LMER specifications. The short page locator does not uniquely establish these dimensions across manuscript and published pagination. No candidate is promoted by numeric matching. All-participant meta-analysis: small-telescopes Z = -5.22 with printed p = < .001 (strict < .001); equivalence Z = -2.42, p = .008. These test different nulls; neither is a test that the beverage effect is zero. Table 2 has BvC fixed-effect coefficients 3.276, 5.849, 5.794 (SEs 1.369, 2.045, 2.045), with p < .05, < .01, < .01 respectively; they are coefficients, not printed t statistics. Model 2 simple effects further report t(45.35) = 2.46, p = .018 among naive participants and t(87.03) = -1.41, p = .161 among suspicious participants. Figures 1 and the subgroup analyses offer additional sample-specific estimates. Sample candidates: Model 1 explicitly has 1137 participant observations; Model 2 has 933 participant observations after excluding three studies lacking hypothesis-knowledge coding; Model 3 has 5502 vignette-rating observations contributed by 933 participants, with 96 missing ratings not imputed. These are candidate model Ns only, not assigned analytic N. General exclusions: four declined data-use consent, three under age 18, three rated fewer than three vignettes, and two had unknown beverage condition. No N inferred from df or recruitment totals, and no N sum or effect conversion performed. The reported-success value codes the authors’ explicit overall narrative conclusion; it does not resolve the target statistical test.
